tunables.label: API Server Enabled
tunables.description: Sample switch for the OpenAI-compatible API server (GET /health and /v1 on port 8642). False by default and it is the sample's real off-switch: while false, the compose boot prelude runs `hermes config set platforms.api_server.enabled false` on every start, so nothing listens on 8642 and no 8642 port is published.
tunables.troubleshooting: Setting this flag alone would NOT disable the API in this upstream build — the gateway gates that adapter on a usable API_SERVER_KEY (>= 16 characters, deny-listed placeholders rejected) and the image's first-boot stage2 hook generates one per data volume (0600, in /opt/data/.env, never committed), so upstream's loopback control plane would otherwise start. The compose `command` prelude is what makes false mean off (and true mean: stop pinning, let upstream's key gate decide). Dashboard-internal cron keeps working while off (the gateway runs its own cron ticker); only the optional external Chronos/NAS cron-fire callback and relay-fronted manual runs need the loopback API. To opt in: set true in `.env`, set HERMES_API_SERVER_HOST=0.0.0.0, uncomment the 8642 publish rule, restart, then verify GET /health and `Authorization: Bearer <key>` on /v1. Manual equivalent: `hermes config unset platforms.api_server.enabled` inside the container.

tunables.label: API Server Bind Address
tunables.description: Host/bind address for the API server once it is opted in; the sample passes HERMES_API_SERVER_HOST through with the upstream default 127.0.0.1 (loopback inside the container). Irrelevant while API_SERVER_ENABLED=false, because then no listener is created at all.
tunables.troubleshooting: The sample does not publish 8642, so the loopback default is fine — and safest, since it would be unreachable from other containers too. To reach the API from the host you must both set this to 0.0.0.0 and uncomment the `- "127.0.0.1:8642:8642"` publish rule (Docker forwards to the container IP, so 127.0.0.1 here leaves a published port dead). API_SERVER_KEY is still required even on loopback binds.

tunables.label: API Server Key
tunables.description: Bearer token clients send to the API server; the gateway refuses to start the adapter without a strong key (minimum 16 characters; a small deny-list of obvious placeholders such as `changeme` is also rejected). Optional in this sample: it defaults to empty, meaning no key material exists in the repository — while the API stays pinned off the key is unused anyway, and the image's first-boot stage2 hook generates a per-volume one (/opt/data/.env, 0600, git-ignored) as soon as you opt in.
tunables.troubleshooting: Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. When opting in you may pin your own value (`openssl rand -hex 32`) as HERMES_API_SERVER_KEY in the git-ignored `.env` (interpolated by `${HERMES_API_SERVER_KEY:-}` in docker-compose.yml) — a container-provided key makes stage2 skip generation; never put a real key in the compose file or the repository. The example string above is a documentation placeholder only and is on upstream's deny-list, so it could never authenticate. Note the API must also be un-pinned (API_SERVER_ENABLED=true) before any key matters.

tunables.label: Hermes Home
tunables.description: Persistent Hermes configuration, state and data directory; must point at the mounted volume (/opt/data).
tunables.troubleshooting: Keep it on the declared /opt/data volume so gateway/API state survives `docker compose down -v` rebuilds; a different path loses profile and provider state.

tunables.label: Unbuffered Python
tunables.description: Writes Python stdout/stderr without buffering so logs appear immediately.
tunables.troubleshooting: Set to true when container logs look delayed or truncated in `docker compose logs`.

tunables.label: Disable Bytecode Files
tunables.description: Prevents Python from writing .pyc bytecode files into the container filesystem.
tunables.troubleshooting: Keep true in read-only or ephemeral root filesystems to avoid write errors on import.

tunables.label: Safe Write Root
tunables.description: Root directory that Hermes is allowed to write to (safe-write guard).
tunables.troubleshooting: Must stay inside the mounted /opt/data volume; writes outside this root are rejected.

tunables.label: Disable Lazy Installs
tunables.description: Disables on-demand package installs so container startup stays deterministic.
tunables.troubleshooting: Leave enabled in containers; disabling allows installs at runtime into HERMES_LAZY_INSTALL_TARGET, which needs network and a writable volume.

tunables.label: API Server Port
tunables.description: Port the OpenAI-compatible API server listens on; must match the published container port. Only relevant after opting in — the sample publishes nothing on 8642.
tunables.troubleshooting: The sample keeps the API off, so this port has no listener and no probe targets it. After opting in, if `/health` times out through a published port, check that the compose mapping (for example 8643:8643) matches this value on both halves and that API_SERVER_HOST is 0.0.0.0.

tunables.label: Anthropic API Key
tunables.description: Anthropic Console API key used when the active model provider is `anthropic`.
tunables.troubleshooting: Without it Hermes falls back to OAuth credentials (Claude Code files / `hermes model`) or the next configured provider; a 401 from api.anthropic.com means the key is missing or expired. Pair with ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL only when routing through a proxy.

tunables.label: Anthropic Base URL
tunables.description: Overrides the Anthropic API base URL, for gateways or corporate proxies.
tunables.troubleshooting: Leave unset for direct Anthropic access; a wrong path (missing `/v1`) yields 404s on every Anthropic request.

tunables.label: OpenAI API Key
tunables.description: API key for OpenAI or any custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint used together with OPENAI_BASE_URL.
tunables.troubleshooting: Only read when `model.provider` selects an OpenAI-compatible provider; a 401 from the endpoint means the key is missing or the provider is misconfigured.

tunables.label: OpenAI Base URL
tunables.description: Base URL for a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint (vLLM, SGLang, LM Studio, local gateway).
tunables.troubleshooting: Point at the `/v1` root; a wrong host or missing `/v1` shows up as connection errors or 404s on completion requests.

tunables.label: OpenRouter API Key
tunables.description: OpenRouter API key; upstream recommends it for access to many models through one credential.
tunables.troubleshooting: Select the provider with `hermes model`; a 401 from openrouter.ai means the key is missing, expired, or has no credit.

tunables.label: Google AI Studio API Key
tunables.description: Google AI Studio API key for Gemini models; GEMINI_API_KEY is an alias for this variable.
tunables.troubleshooting: Vertex AI does not use this key — it needs VERTEX_CREDENTIALS_PATH (service-account JSON) instead. A 403 usually means the key lacks Generative Language API access.

tunables.label: Gemini API Key
tunables.description: Alias for GOOGLE_API_KEY; used interchangeably by the Google/Gemini provider.
tunables.troubleshooting: Setting only one of GOOGLE_API_KEY / GEMINI_API_KEY is enough; if both are set, keep them identical to avoid confusing provider diagnostics.

tunables.label: DeepSeek API Key
tunables.description: DeepSeek API key for direct DeepSeek access.
tunables.troubleshooting: Override DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL when using a relay; a 402/429 from DeepSeek means account balance or rate limits, not a container problem.

tunables.label: Groq API Key
tunables.description: Groq API key; upstream consumes it for Groq Whisper speech-to-text (and Groq-backed model access).
tunables.troubleshooting: Voice features stay silent without it — set STT_GROQ_MODEL only if you also need a non-default model (`whisper-large-v3-turbo` is the default).

tunables.label: xAI API Key
tunables.description: xAI (Grok) API key for chat, TTS and web search.
tunables.troubleshooting: xAI_BASE_URL defaults to https://api.x.ai/v1; only override it for a proxy. A 401 means the key is missing or the project has no credits.

tunables.label: Telegram Bot Token
tunables.description: Telegram bot token from @BotFather; enables the Telegram gateway adapter.
tunables.troubleshooting: Without a token the gateway skips Telegram entirely. If the bot is added to groups but stays silent, also set TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS (and TELEGRAM_GROUP_ALLOWED_CHATS for forums).

tunables.label: Telegram Allowed Users
tunables.description: Comma-separated Telegram user IDs allowed to use the bot in DMs, groups and forums.
tunables.troubleshooting: Unset, the bot does not accept anyone (except with TELEGRAM_ALLOW_ALL_USERS, which is dev-only). Get your numeric user ID from @userinfobot; never use allow-all on a public deployment.

tunables.label: Discord Bot Token
tunables.description: Discord bot token; enables the Discord gateway adapter.
tunables.troubleshooting: A 4001/invalid-token error means the token was reset in the Developer Portal. The bot also needs the Message Content intent enabled in Discord, otherwise messages arrive empty.

tunables.label: Discord Allowed Users
tunables.description: Comma-separated Discord user IDs allowed to use the bot (DISCORD_ALLOWED_ROLES grants access by role instead).
tunables.troubleshooting: Messages are ignored until at least one user, role or channel is allowed; DISCORD_ALLOW_ALL_USERS exists for development only.

tunables.label: Slack Bot Token
tunables.description: Slack bot token (`xoxb-...`) used by the Slack adapter.
tunables.troubleshooting: Slack runs in Socket Mode, so this must be paired with SLACK_APP_TOKEN (`xapp-...`); without the app token the adapter cannot open its connection.

tunables.label: Slack App Token
tunables.description: Slack app-level token (`xapp-...`) required for Socket Mode.
tunables.troubleshooting: Generate it with `connections:write` scope on the Slack app; a `xapp_`/`xoxb_` mix-up is the usual cause of a failed handshake.

tunables.label: Slack Allowed Users
tunables.description: Comma-separated Slack user IDs allowed to trigger the bot.
tunables.troubleshooting: Unset, the bot only responds where SLACK_ALLOW_ALL_USERS or free-response channel rules apply; find IDs with `slack users list`.

tunables.label: Enable Web Dashboard
tunables.description: Starts the supervised web dashboard service (default port 9119) inside the container; the sample's only published port and the target of the container healthcheck.
tunables.troubleshooting: Unset/`false`, the s6 dashboard service exits immediately (finish script marks it down) and nothing listens on 9119 — and because the healthcheck probes the dashboard, the container then stays permanently unhealthy (remove or repoint the healthcheck block if you deliberately run without it). Set to `1` to start it, and note the default container bind 0.0.0.0 is non-loopback: upstream then engages its auth gate and exits unless an auth provider is registered, so a basic-auth pair (HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_USERNAME + _PASSWORD) or OAuth (HERMES_DASHBOARD_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID) is required for the dashboard to come up at all. The sample enables it with a placeholder basic-auth pair and publishes 127.0.0.1:9119 only; replace the password in `.env` before widening the publish rule. HERMES_DASHBOARD_INSECURE is accepted but ignored — it no longer disables the gate.

tunables.label: Dashboard Bind Address
tunables.description: Bind address for the dashboard HTTP server.
tunables.troubleshooting: A loopback bind is unreachable from outside the container — Docker's published port forwards to the container IP, so 127.0.0.1 here leaves 9119 unreachable even with a port mapping. Keep 0.0.0.0 for published traffic; that non-loopback bind engages the auth gate, which needs a provider (basic auth or OAuth) or startup fails closed.

tunables.label: Dashboard Port
tunables.description: Port for the dashboard HTTP server; must match the published container port.
tunables.troubleshooting: If the dashboard URL is unreachable, confirm the compose mapping matches this value and that HERMES_DASHBOARD is truthy with an auth provider configured. The sample publishes 127.0.0.1:9119:9119 (host loopback); widen the left side only after replacing the placeholder password.

tunables.label: Dashboard Basic Auth Username
tunables.description: Username for the bundled username/password dashboard-auth provider (`dashboard_auth/basic`); activates it when set together with a password. Login happens through the dashboard sign-in form (`GET /login`, JSON `POST /auth/password-login`) — the dashboard does not accept an HTTP `Authorization: Basic` header.
tunables.troubleshooting: Setting only the username is a no-op — both HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_USERNAME and a password (or password hash) are required before the auth gate turns on. The sample supplies `admin` as a placeholder; override it with the other basic-auth values via `.env` (see `.env.example`). Test with `curl -sI http://127.0.0.1:9119/` (expects 302 to `/login`) rather than `curl -u`, which the form login ignores.

tunables.label: Dashboard Basic Auth Password
tunables.description: Password for the dashboard sign-in form (scrypt-hashed in memory at load); wins over a configured password_hash so it can be rotated via env.
tunables.troubleshooting: The example is a local-only placeholder — replace it before any real deployment; the sample compose carries the same placeholder behind `${HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_PASSWORD:-...}` so the real value lives in a git-ignored `.env`. Basic auth is suitable for a trusted LAN/VPN only; use HERMES_DASHBOARD_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID for public exposure. Sessions also need HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_SECRET to survive restarts.

tunables.label: Dashboard Session Secret
tunables.description: Signing key for dashboard basic-auth session cookies (base64, hex or raw text; decoded length of 16+ bytes is accepted). Empty means upstream generates a random per-process key.
tunables.troubleshooting: Without it every container start mints a new key, so logged-in sessions die on restart and cannot span workers — set 32+ random bytes (`openssl rand -base64 32`) in `.env` for stable sessions. The sample passes an empty value, i.e. it keeps the upstream default and ships no secret.

tunables.label: Disable AWS IMDS Probe
tunables.description: Skips the botocore instance-metadata (169.254.169.254) credential probe that `model.provider: auto` triggers during gateway startup.
tunables.troubleshooting: On hosts outside AWS the IMDS connect can blackhole indefinitely, so `gateway run` never finishes startup and the gateway daemon is not supervising anything (the dashboard on 9119 is independent and still comes up). Set true for container samples that do not use Bedrock; only unset on real EC2/ECS where instance-role credentials are wanted.

tunables.label: Runtime User ID
tunables.description: Host UID the s6 stage2 hook remaps the internal `hermes` user to before services start; matches ownership of the mounted /opt/data volume.
tunables.troubleshooting: Permission errors on the mounted volume mean this does not match the host directory owner — run `id -u` on the host and set it (or PUID) on every container start, including throwaway diagnostic containers.

tunables.label: Runtime Group ID
tunables.description: Host GID paired with HERMES_UID for remapping the internal `hermes` group.
tunables.troubleshooting: Keep it consistent with the host group of /opt/data (`id -g`); a mismatch shows up as group-readable-but-not-writable files after a rebuild.

tunables.label: Runtime User ID (alias)
tunables.description: Alias for HERMES_UID, provided for parity with LinuxServer.io and NAS images.
tunables.troubleshooting: If both are set, prefer HERMES_UID so there is one source of truth; either one prevents the UID-10000-takes-over-the-volume failure mode.

tunables.label: Runtime Group ID (alias)
tunables.description: Alias for HERMES_GID, provided for parity with LinuxServer.io and NAS images.
tunables.troubleshooting: Set it together with PUID; leaving GID unmapped on a group-owned volume reproduces the same permission errors as an unmatched UID.

notes: Dashboard-first sample: the only published port is 127.0.0.1:9119 (host loopback) for the web dashboard started by the s6 dashboard service when HERMES_DASHBOARD is truthy (HERMES_DASHBOARD_PORT default 9119). Because the dashboard's default container bind is 0.0.0.0 (non-loopback), upstream's auth gate applies and startup fails closed without an auth provider — a basic-auth pair or OAuth client id is required for it to start; the sample enables it with a placeholder basic-auth pair and an empty HERMES_DASHBOARD_BASIC_AUTH_SECRET (upstream's random per-process default). Probes and the compose healthcheck therefore target the dashboard: unauthenticated GET / must answer the login redirect (302 with Location pointing at /login; a 200 also counts), matching what a browser sees — connection refused or 4xx/5xx marks the container unhealthy, and HERMES_DASHBOARD=0 makes it permanently unhealthy unless the healthcheck is repointed. Upstream additionally exposes an unauthenticated GET /api/health on 9119 as its own liveness endpoint. The OpenAI-compatible API server (8642, API_SERVER_PORT default 8642, GET /health) is opt-in and off by default: while API_SERVER_ENABLED=false the compose `command` boot prelude pins platforms.api_server.enabled=false in config.yaml on every start, and no 8642 publish rule exists, so nothing listens on 8642 inside or outside the container. That prelude — not the flag or an empty key — is the effective off-switch: the flag is declarative in this build, the gateway gates the adapter on a usable API_SERVER_KEY (>= 16 chars), and the image's first-boot stage2 hook generates one per data volume anyway (0600, /opt/data/.env, git-ignored) to serve upstream's loopback control plane. Dashboard-internal cron keeps working while the API is off (the gateway runs its own cron ticker); only the optional external Chronos/NAS cron-fire callback and relay-fronted manual runs need the loopback API, which API_SERVER_ENABLED=true restores (together with HERMES_API_SERVER_HOST=0.0.0.0 and the uncommented publish rule for external access). Credentials are interpolated from a git-ignored `.env` (`${...}` in docker-compose.yml, template in `.env.example`) — only local-only placeholders live in the repository, the API key default is deliberately empty so no key material is ever committed, and none of the provider keys or messaging tokens below is supplied by the sample. Provider credentials and messaging tokens are read from the process environment or `~/.hermes/.env` (prefer `config.yaml` for non-secret behaviour); every credential in `tunables` is optional and carries a placeholder example only.
